Text of Letter (PDF)

Washington, D.C. — Representative Becca Balint (VT-AL), a member of the House Subcommittee on the Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust and U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) demanded answers from McDonald’s President and CEO Chris Kempczinski about how the company generates AI-driven pricing recommendations, whether McDonald’s pressures franchisees to follow them, and how the company assesses the technology’s potential harm to consumers and competition. The letter came after reports that the company is using artificial intelligence (AI) to determine the “optimal price” for individual menu items at each of its locations and pushing franchisees to adopt these AI-based prices.

“We are concerned that McDonald’s may be using AI to squeeze consumers into paying higher prices, and that its AI pricing tools may facilitate collusion between franchisees who should be operating as competitors,” wrote the lawmakers.

U.S. Representatives Greg Casar (D-Texas), Jesús “Chuy” García (D-Ill.), and Mary Gay Scanlon (D-Pa.) also signed the letter.

According to recent reports, McDonald’s has developed an AI-based pricing tool that it may be using to recommend specific prices for each individual store, building off the massive trove of consumer data that Amazon has collected through its loyalty program and mobile app. For example, two McDonald’s-operated restaurants just two miles apart in Fresno, California reportedly charged prices that differed by as much as 21 percent for the same menu items. The lawmakers raised particular concerns about McDonald’s use of AI-based pricing at a time when food prices are rising nationwide and particularly at McDonald’s. One report found that certain McDonald’s menu prices doubled between 2014 and 2024, rising more than three times as fast as overall inflation and driving away customers who previously relied on McDonald’s for an affordable meal.

“We are concerned that McDonald’s is using its extensive consumer data and algorithmic pricing tools to unfairly raise prices on consumers who are already struggling with high food and dining costs,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers also questioned McDonald’s for reportedly putting pressure on franchisees to adopt its pricing recommendations, including through new business standards and potential consequences for franchise renewals. They warned that encouraging competing franchisees to rely on a shared pricing tool informed by nonpublic data could undermine independent pricing decisions and raise antitrust concerns.

“While McDonald’s asserts that using data and analytics to inform pricing is a standard business practice, pressuring competing franchisees to use a shared AI pricing tool built on nonpublic data is not a standard business practice, but rather a potential antitrust issue,” continued the lawmakers.

The lawmakers requested answers by November 16, 2026, on the data and algorithms used to generate pricing recommendations, the extent to which franchisees adopt those recommendations, the pressure McDonald’s places on franchisees to comply, and the company’s assessment of potential antitrust risks.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Ted W. Lieu (D-Los Angeles County) issued the following statement after being re-elected to serve California’s 36th congressional district in the U.S. House of Representatives for the 120th Congress.

“Today, I want to express my deepest gratitude to the residents of California’s 36th congressional district for once again placing their trust in me to represent them in Congress. Serving our beautiful community is truly the honor of my lifetime. I am incredibly grateful to my family, whose support means everything to me.

“But the work is just beginning. Democrats will enter the new Congress ready to fight for American families. The American people have spoken and have emphatically repudiated the MAGA agenda of trump and Republicans.

“With a united House and Senate, Democrats will focus on bringing down costs. We will work to reverse trump and Republicans’ reckless tariffs, end their illegal war in Iran, and undo their cruel cuts to health care and food assistance. We will also hold the trump administration accountable for its corruption, abuses of power, and blatant violations of the law. We will advance an affirmative agenda that safeguards election integrity, reinforces states’ ability to prepare for and respond to natural disasters, and puts reasonable guardrails on AI. We will treat our neighbors with respect and dignity, not division and contempt.

“I do not take this re-election, or the trust of my constituents, for granted. I promise to bring everything I have to the fight for an America that puts working families first.”

(Washington, DC) — This morning, Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) made the following statement after Democrats secured the majority of the House and Senate in the 2026 midterm election:

“Yesterday, the American people chose stability over chaos,” said Ranking Member Lofgren. “They chose people and policies that will make not only their lives better, but the lives of future generations better. Americans chose science and reason. They’ve put their trust in Democrats and our ability to deliver on our promises.

She continued: “I will be seeking the Chair of the House Science Committee. First and foremost, as Chairwoman, I will work to put a stop to Trump’s politicization of science. We will hold this administration accountable for the damage they have done to the American scientific enterprise. The oversight and investigations work we’ve been doing for the past two years in the minority will continue. We have a lot of work to do, and we’ll be ready to hit the ground running come the start of the 120th Congress, with Democrats in control of the House and Senate.

“We will also set out to fix what Trump has broken. We’ll restore and advance support for our premiere science institutions and the dedicated people who work there. We will build protections for federal science and innovation programs so Trump-era corruption cannot happen again.

“The future is unfolding before us with groundbreaking technologies like AI, quantum, and fusion energy. We need to build responsible regulations for AI while also fostering innovation. We must invest holistically in quantum to meet emerging challenges for our competitiveness in this field. This administration’s climate denialism has set us back. We need to advance climate solutions now. Fusion, with its limitless, emission-free power, will help us achieve our clean energy future. Breakthrough after breakthrough in fusion energy science has been encouraging—and we need to match this momentum with federal support.

“The U.S. research ecosystem used to be the envy of the world. People brought their ideas and energy here—and our Nation reaped the rewards of that talent in discoveries and the resulting economic growth. That is now all at risk. I will stop at nothing to earn back the trust of our allies across the globe, end the brain drain, restore scientific integrity across our agencies, and reaffirm our leadership in science. The American people deserve no less.”

Financial services driven by artificial intelligence and round-the-clock payments systems may contribute to and rapidly spread financial stress. As the financial system accelerates, real-time information and automated tools can help institutions and regulators respond faster, improve access to liquidity, and better prepare for orderly bank resolutions. Meanwhile, advances in AI are creating new cybersecurity threats. Through enhanced collective maintenance and security built in from the start, open-source software can provide stronger protection against cyber threats. Model open-source software also has the potential to lower development and reporting costs for community banks and credit unions and expand their access to advanced risk-management capabilities.

The Real-Time Regulatory Study Act directs the Federal Reserve Board, in coordination with other financial regulators, to develop, test, and publicly release open-source demonstration software to evaluate how technology can streamline regulatory obligations, reduce compliance costs, and provide regulators with real-time information on the condition of financial institutions nationwide. The Federal Reserve would seek technical contributions from financial institutions, technology providers, open-source organizations, and researchers.

matches.text:
NOBLESVILLE, IN — Congresswoman Victoria Spartz (IN-05) is calling for sweeping federal and state investigations into utility surcharges, corporate subsidies, energy infrastructure costs, threats to grid reliability, and the use of eminent domain for projects benefiting private corporations.

In three letters to the Government Accountability Office (GAO), the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and Department of Energy (DOE), and Indiana’s new legislative leadership, Spartz is demanding independent audits, stronger property rights, greater transparency, and meaningful regulatory reforms.

“Americans are being forced to bankroll a system where powerful utilities collect guaranteed returns, wealthy corporations receive massive subsidies, and hardworking families and small businesses get stuck with higher bills,” said Rep. Spartz. “It is time to follow the money and expose who approved these sweetheart deals, who profited, and who got stuck with the bill.”

Spartz is demanding action on:

Utility surcharges, no-bid contracts, and corporate subsidies: Audit previously approved federal and state utility surcharges, special rate riders, guaranteed returns, no-bid contracts and preferential transmission development rights, tax breaks, and corporate incentives to determine whether costs were justified or improperly passed on to consumers.

Eminent domain and property rights: Reform laws allowing private property to be taken for transmission projects primarily benefiting corporate interests. Require proof of genuine public necessity, independent review of alternatives, and fair treatment of affected landowners.

Cost shifting: Require data centers and other major electricity users to pay their full generation, transmission, and infrastructure costs rather than shifting them onto families and small businesses.

Grid reliability and blackouts: Examine whether rapidly expanding electricity demand, premature power plant retirements, and delays in new generation and transmission threaten reliable electricity supplies. Develop a concrete plan for dependable natural gas and nuclear generation.

Energy costs and environmental risks: Investigate the full costs and potential pollution risks of solar, wind, and battery storage projects, including their effects on utility bills and grid reliability.

Regulatory failures: Investigate PJM and MISO governance, utility conflicts of interest, regulatory compliance failures, and national security concerns. Reform the structure, transparency, and accountability of Indiana’s Utility Regulatory Commission.

Farmland, water, and public safety: Protect productive farmland and water resources, investigate publicly subsidized infrastructure, and examine the safety of battery storage facilities proposed in flood-prone areas.

Transparency and accountability: Require independent verification of electricity demand, competitive transmission development, disclosure of financial beneficiaries, and enforceable protections against abandoned projects and stranded costs.

“We are shutting down reliable power plants while rushing to approve massive new electricity loads without adequate generation. Who is planning for the blackouts? Who is paying for the infrastructure? And who is holding these regulators accountable?” Spartz continued.

“Eminent domain must serve genuine public necessity—not become a tool for wealthy corporations to seize farmland and force families to subsidize their private developments.”

Spartz is requesting a comprehensive GAO investigation of historical utility charges and corporate incentives, federal regulatory action on large-load projects and grid reliability, and legislative reforms by Indiana’s General Assembly when it reconvenes in January.

“Indiana families should not be subsidizing billionaires’ data centers through hidden utility charges and government handouts. We need a full accounting of every dollar, independent audits, and recovery of any improper payments.”

“This is corporate welfare on the backs of American taxpayers and ratepayers. Enough is enough. Government must stop protecting powerful special interests and start protecting the people who pay the bills.”

The three letters address:

GAO: Independent investigation and audits of utility surcharges, subsidies, infrastructure costs, regulatory failures, and potential improper cost recovery. See letter HERE.

FERC and DOE: Federal action on large-load developments, grid reliability, transmission competition, generation planning, and regional grid governance. See letter HERE.
